title: lateral-ic-rapid-transfer-12day-immersion-and-mentor-log
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, low-friction 12-day immersion plan for lateral IC transfers (engineers or product folks moving between pods). Goal = reduce ramp friction, preserve institutional knowledge, and validate pairwise competency transfer without a long formal shadow.

Audience:
People Ops + hiring manager + intake mentor + receiving team mentor. Use when someone is transferring internally (no new hire paperwork) but needs an accelerated handoff.

Quick notes / assumptions (notes to self):
- Not for senior manager role swaps; for ICs (IC2–IC4).
- Manager must allocate 2x 1-hr mentor sessions during week 1.
- Backfill access requests to be made before day 0 (ticket HR-783).
- Keep things asynchronous where possible: recorded screen snippets, doc snippets.

Success signals (what good looks like after 12 days):
- New role owner can (with mentor present) complete the primary onboarding task or PR review end-to-end at least once.
- Access and tooling: dev env + CI access + Slack channel access + calendar group are working.
- Mentor notes show at most 3 open knowledge gaps (documented) not blocking delivery.
- Receiving PM/EM comfortable to move them into weekly cadence.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: access gaps slow learning —> Mitigation: access audit 48h pre-transfer. (Owner: People Ops)
- Risk: no mentor availability —> Mitigation: assign backup mentor and async materials.
- Risk: context fragmentation —> Mitigation: use the single "handoff capsule" doc (link: confluence:ONBOARD-2543).

12-day immersion outline (compact):
Pre-day 0 (T-minus):
- Checklist: hardware, VPN, SSO groups, GH org invite, CI token, Slack invite. Ticket: JIRA:HR-783.
- Create handoff capsule: 300–600 words summary + 3 primary artifacts (PR/diagrams/dataschema) uploaded to confluence:ONBOARD-2543.
- People Ops sends welcome + intro template to receiving team slack (see templates below).

Day 0–1: orientation + map
- 60m intro with receiving manager (role expectations, immediate priorities).
- 45m mentor meet (context map: what systems, where docs live, past incidents).
- Access verification checklist run (owner: mentee, proctored by mentor).
- Quick task: clone repo, run dev server. Log: success/fail + blockers.

Day 2–3: observe + tiny ship
- Observe mentor doing a canonical task (30–60m screen share; record).
- Tiny ship assignment: non-critical bug/typo/infra test that touches codebase or docs. Aim: end-to-end cycle < 4h.
- Debrief 30m with mentor: what felt unclear. Capture 3 action items.

Day 4–6: pair deeper + review rubric
- Pair program for 2 x 2h sessions (mentor+mentee) on different subsystems.
- Interview-style rubric check: run through 6 probe questions (see rubric below), grade evidence.
- Deliverable: annotated PR addressing feedback from pair sessions.

Day 7–9: independent delivery with backup
- Mentee leads a medium-scope task with mentor on-call for questions (mentor watches asynchronously).
- Postmortem-lite: 30m write-up of choices + 1 diagram. Link to confluence capsule.
- Manager check-in (15m) to confirm alignment with next 30d objectives.

Day 10–12: closeout + transition to weekly cadence
- Final demo to receiving team (20–30m).
- Mentor fills mentor-log (template below) and marks open items.
- Handoff capsule updated and flagged to manager; change owner from mentor->receiving manager.

Interview / knowledge-transfer rubric (used by mentor during Day 4–6):
Scoring: 0 | 1 | 2  (0 = no evidence, 1 = partial, 2 = solid evidence)
- System comprehension: can describe the high-level data flow and main services (evidence: 2 if can sketch diagram + name teams).
- Ownership patterns: can explain deployment and rollback process (evidence: 2 if walked through a rollback in staging).
- Debugging trace: can reproduce a typical production incident locally or via logs (evidence: 2 if reproduced).
- Code hygiene: can open a PR with tests and passing CI (evidence: PR link).
- Cross-team communications: can write an async update for 3rd-party team (evidence: draft message).
- Risk awareness: identifies top 2 operational risks and mitigations for the service (evidence: bullet list).

Templates (copy and tweak):
- Welcome slack DM (people-ops -> receiving channel):
  "Hi @team, Maya here from People Ops. Quick heads up: @Name is transferring into your team today. Primary focus: X. Mentor: @Mentor. Please add to #team-standup and grant GH/CI access by EOD. If questions ping: #people-ops-onboard."

- Mentor log (short):
  "Mentee: [name] | DayRange: 0–12 | Primary artifacts: [PR links] | Scores: [list 6 numbers] | Open items: [3 bullets] | Recommended next-steps: [3 bullets]"

- 1:1 starter agenda (first two weeks):
  "1) Quick wins / blockers (10m) 2) Knowledge handoff questions (10m) 3) Traffic lights: confidence/risks (5m) 4) Action items + owner (5m)"

Practical checklists (short):
- Access quick audit (pass/fail checklist): GH org, CI token, cloud_console_read, prod_log_view, slack channels, calendar group.
- Dev env smoke test: clone -> install -> start -> run tests (must pass baseline sample). Log terminal output to confluence snippet.

Documentation hygiene rules (to reduce future ramp cost):
- Every handoff capsule must include: 1) 300-word overview, 2) 1 diagram (PNG/SVG), 3) 2 example PRs, 4) troubleshooting steps for top 3 incidents.
- Tag capsule with team tag + "handoff-YYYYMMDD".

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Should we enforce a mandatory checklist gate in the transfer workflow (JIRA hook)? pros/cons. (Discuss w/ eng-ops).
- Where to store short screencasts so they are searchable — currently using confluence attachments but indexing is weak. (Samir to investigate cloud video host).
- Decide if manager must sign-off on rubric score >= 8/12 to be considered "operational".

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally lightweight — the goal is to make lateral moves low friction. Keep the plan iterative; first draft for internal trial cohort.
- Feedback loop: please add comments inline on confluence:ONBOARD-2543 and tag @Maya for follow-up.

Appendix: example micro-task (for Day 2):
- Fix flaky unit test X that blocks mainline CI. Steps: run test_locally.sh -> reproduce -> add deterministic seed -> open PR. Estimated time: 1–3h.

End.
